sources.t: Codes of practice
sources.f: Updated 16 July 2025; Ofcom indexes complaint-handling, automatic-compensation and broadband-speed voluntary codes and participating providers.
sources.g: Codes and signatory status describe consumer protections, not exact network reach at a premises.

sources.t: Switching mobile phone provider
sources.f: Updated 1 July 2026; Ofcom explains Text to Switch, PAC and STAC processes and compensation for delayed mobile switching.
sources.g: Mobile switching rules do not establish fixed-broadband availability or parcel connectivity.

sources.t: Switching mobile, broadband or landline
sources.f: Updated 1 July 2026; the official hub links current switching processes for mobile, broadband and landline services.
sources.g: Switching guidance presupposes selectable services and is not independent exact-address evidence.

sources.t: What happens to your email address when you switch broadband provider
sources.f: Updated 10 June 2025; Ofcom compares major-provider policies for retaining provider-issued email addresses after switching.
sources.g: Email retention policy is an account-service issue and does not prove broadband network reach.

sources.t: 1.6 million Brits hit switch on their landline or broadband provider
sources.f: Published 12 September 2025; Ofcom reported more than 1.6 million One Touch Switch uses during its first year.
sources.g: National switching totals are aggregate consumer behaviour, not premises-level serviceability evidence.

sources.t: Statement: Quick, easy and reliable switching
sources.f: Updated 4 December 2024; Ofcom records its One Touch Switch decisions and General Condition implementation framework.
sources.g: Regulatory switching requirements do not confirm current provider availability at an address.

sources.t: Emergency video relay
sources.f: Published 31 March 2023; Ofcom explains the free 24-hour emergency video relay service for deaf British Sign Language users.
sources.g: Emergency-service accessibility requires a connected device but does not establish parcel broadband orderability.

sources.t: Ex post evaluation of our emergency video relay regulation
sources.f: Updated 5 September 2025; Ofcom evaluated use and outcomes of the emergency video relay regulation introduced in 2022.
sources.g: Service-use and accessibility outcomes are not fixed-network coverage evidence for a premises.

sources.t: Communications services for disabled people
sources.f: Official guidance describes provider accessibility services, directory information and emergency relay support for disabled people.
sources.g: Accessibility obligations and support services do not establish exact-address connectivity.

sources.t: Access and inclusion research
sources.f: Updated 30 July 2024; Ofcom groups research on access, ownership, digital exclusion, affordability, engagement and complaints among potentially vulnerable consumers.
sources.g: Survey and inclusion research is population-level context, not live parcel service evidence.

sources.t: Compliance programme into access to emergency services
sources.f: Closed 8 June 2026; Ofcom assessed compliance with emergency-call access and caller-location obligations under the General Conditions.
sources.g: Compliance monitoring for voice providers does not prove broadband orderability at a premises.

sources.t: Amendments to the General Conditions of Entitlement
sources.f: Updated 22 April 2025; the page indexes amendments including One Touch Switch and accessibility-related General Condition changes.
sources.g: Regulatory amendments describe provider duties rather than physical network reach.

sources.t: UK Gigabit Programme: Norfolk Public Review
sources.f: Updated 23 June 2026; the consultation page publishes Norfolk Public Review outcome material and postcode-level supporting files.
sources.g: Public Review classifications combine existing and planned infrastructure and are not live retail order checks.

sources.t: Norfolk Lot 7 Public Review Closure Notice
sources.f: Updated in 2026; BDUK records redesign of the Norfolk contract to around 33,000 premises following commercial-rollout changes.
sources.g: Redesigned contract scope is programme evidence, not proof of current service at a parcel.

sources.t: Project Gigabit Programme: Shropshire Public Review
sources.f: The consultation records Shropshire Public Review outcomes following an Open Market Review of existing and planned gigabit infrastructure.
sources.g: Historic consultation and intervention mapping require fresh UPRN and provider validation.

sources.t: UK Gigabit Programme: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Public Review
sources.f: Updated 24 February 2025; the page publishes Hampshire Public Review closure and revised postcode materials.
sources.g: Public Review outcome files do not establish present retail availability for an address.

sources.t: Hampshire Lot 27 Public Review Closure Notice
sources.f: Updated in 2026; BDUK records a redesigned Hampshire contract covering around 29,000 premises after market changes.
sources.g: Programme redesign and investment totals are not current parcel orderability evidence.

sources.t: Project Gigabit - Dorset and South Somerset Lot 14 Public Review
sources.f: The consultation outcome publishes Dorset and South Somerset intervention-area and postcode materials following a 2022 Public Review.
sources.g: Historic Public Review outputs are procurement context and not live exact-address service evidence.

sources.t: Project Gigabit - Mid/East Devon and West Somerset Lot 6 Public Review
sources.f: Updated 29 August 2023; the consultation publishes closure, intervention-area and postcode-level outcome materials.
sources.g: Outcome mapping combines historic and planned coverage and needs current provider validation.

sources.t: Project Gigabit - Cheshire Lot 17 Public Review
sources.f: Updated 14 January 2026; the page publishes Cheshire closure and revised intervention-area materials.
sources.g: Public Review and revised intervention scope do not prove active service at a premises.
